nindian-polity-37-11.s: Judicial review, unlike public health, sanitation and water supply, is a function of:
nindian-polity-37-11.x: Public health, sanitation and water supply are local functions; judicial review belongs to the higher courts.

n0c00af1d6f1.s: Which dimension of decentralisation transfers the power to spend and raise funds and taxes?
n0c00af1d6f1.x: Fiscal decentralisation concerns spending and raising funds and taxes; political concerns deciding, administrative concerns implementing.

nef4c0f04100.s: In India's decentralisation experience, which power was transferred the least to local governments?
nef4c0f04100.x: India transferred political power, some administrative power and the least fiscal power - the decentralisation gap.

nindian-polity-37-3.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Local accountability – decisions at the apex
Local Self-Government – exercise in democratic decentralisation
nindian-polity-37-3.x: Local self-government is democratic decentralisation because it brings community participation and local accountability.

nbaa06fe3026.s: The Nehruvian approach to state and development favoured:
o: A centralised planned state with heavy industry
Cottage industries as the basis of planning
Complete fiscal autonomy for village panchayats
nbaa06fe3026.x: Nehru favoured a centralised planned state with heavy industry (National Planning Committee, Bombay Plan); self-sufficient villages were Gandhi's idea.

n79502f512e0.s: In India, the risk of elite capture by locally dominant castes was cited as an argument for:
n79502f512e0.x: Elite capture by dominant local castes was cited in favour of centralisation, not decentralisation.

n0f83e13e352.s: Which committee recommended constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions, which the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee did not?
n0f83e13e352.x: Balwant Rai Mehta sought a three-tier system, genuine transfer of power and adequate resources; constitutional status came with the L.M. Singhvi Committee.

n510b8c9cae9.s: On which date did Andhra Pradesh follow Rajasthan in introducing Panchayati Raj?
n510b8c9cae9.x: Rajasthan inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959; Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1959.

n5a95dc0f0f2.s: Along with democratic decentralisation, which was a fundamental objective of Panchayati Raj?
n5a95dc0f0f2.x: The fundamental objectives were people's participation in development and democratic decentralisation; financial mobilisation was not one.

nbaf16d596ee.s: After the 73rd Amendment, effective Panchayati Raj needs decentralisation of decision-making, of administrative powers and of:
nbaf16d596ee.x: The needs identified are decentralisation of decision-making, administrative powers and the system as a whole - not judicial powers.

nda0d1d556c6.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Kerala's People's Plan Campaign is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: People's Plan Campaign 2.0 – T.M. Thomas Isaac
People's Plan Campaign 2.0 – student internships and an online portal
nda0d1d556c6.x: About 35-40% of plan funds were devolved, not 60-70%; the other pairs are correct.

n8279ba9e9f8.s: Which Five Year Plan gave Panchayati Raj Institutions a new lease of life but never became an official Plan of India?
n8279ba9e9f8.x: The Janata Government's Sixth Plan (1978-83) revived PRIs but was dropped after 1980 and never became an official Plan.

na75fc8ec952.s: The National Extension Service, which supported the Community Development Programme, was launched in:
na75fc8ec952.x: The NES was launched in 1953 and supported the Community Development Programme of 1952.

n716b44114d3.s: Under the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's model, which tier was to be directly elected?
n716b44114d3.x: Only the village Panchayat was directly elected; the Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad were indirectly elected.

n82f9aded846.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended that the Panchayat Samiti be a/an:
n82f9aded846.x: The Panchayat Samiti was to be the executive body; the Zila Parishad was advisory, coordinating and supervisory.

nf247d60e415.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the decline of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: Excessive independence from the development administration
nf247d60e415.x: Poor finances and irregular elections and supersession were causes; the problem was bureaucratic detachment, not excessive independence.

n32f80dd1c47.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a Panchayati Raj structure of:
o: Two tiers with a four-year term
Three tiers with a four-year term
Two tiers with a five-year term
Three tiers with a five-year term
n32f80dd1c47.x: The Committee proposed replacing the three-tier structure with a two-tier system with a four-year term.

n8162fe4ce15.s: On elections to Panchayati Raj bodies, the Ashok Mehta Committee recommended:
o: Official participation of political parties at all levels
Party participation only at the district level
Party participation only at the village level
n8162fe4ce15.x: The Committee wanted official participation of political parties at all levels of panchayat elections, not a non-party basis.

n3939b7887bf.s: Which committee recommended a District Development Commissioner as Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad?
n3939b7887bf.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee made the district the basic planning unit and proposed a DDC as CEO of the Zila Parishad.

n2f3dc92c925.s: The ideas of which committee served as the model for the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill?
n2f3dc92c925.x: The Gadgil Committee (1988) recommended constitutional status, direct elections and reservations, and was the model for the 64th Bill.

n29d43c39a0f.s: The R.R. Diwakar Committee (1963) dealt with:
n29d43c39a0f.x: R.R. Diwakar (1963) dealt with the Gram Sabha; Nyaya Panchayats was G.R. Rajagopalan and PR Administration was Vishwa Raman.

n22000bd179a.s: Which committee proposed the District Collector as chairman of the Zila Parishad?
n22000bd179a.x: Balwant Rai Mehta made the Collector chairman of the Zila Parishad; later committees such as Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao cut the Collector's development role.

nf7d45f91f73.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Social education – National Adult Education Programme
nf7d45f91f73.x: Social education (adult literacy, community centres) was a component of the Community Development Programme, not of NAEP, IRDP or the NLM.

nc079fab7b41.s: The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989 because it:
o: Had not been passed by the Lok Sabha
Lapsed on dissolution of the Lok Sabha
Failed to secure the special majority
nc079fab7b41.x: Moved by the Rajiv Gandhi Government in July 1989, the Bill passed the Lok Sabha but failed to get the special majority in the Rajya Sabha.

n09abb0e75f5.s: On the Panchayati Raj pattern, the National Development Council decided that:
o: States could vary the pattern, keeping the basic principles common
Every State must adopt an identical pattern
Only Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh could set up Panchayats
Nominated bodies would replace elected ones
n09abb0e75f5.x: The NDC did not insist on one rigid pattern; States could vary it, but the basic principles were common.

n86166380141.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee's two-tier model was:
n86166380141.x: The two-tier model was never adopted nationally; the 73rd Amendment kept a three-tier framework.

new.s: Shifting work to field offices of the same government, with the Centre keeping full control, is called:
new.x: Deconcentration moves work to field offices of the same government and is the weakest form.

new.s: Which form of decentralisation, given effect by the 73rd and 74th Amendments, is the strongest?
new.x: Devolution gives powers to elected local governments with their own mandate and revenue, not withdrawable at will.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about decentralisation:
1. Political decentralisation transfers the power to decide to elected local bodies.
2. Administrative decentralisation transfers the power to implement through staff and functions.
3. Deconcentration is the strongest form of decentralisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; deconcentration is the weakest form, devolution the strongest.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of local government?
new.x: Public health, sanitation and rural development are local functions; public order is not.

new.s: Which of the following was an argument for decentralisation in India?
o: Planned heavy industry needs a single command
Food security needs a single command
new.x: Proximity to local needs argues for decentralisation; heavy industry, food security and elite capture were arguments for centralisation.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an argument for decentralisation?
new.x: Weak local capacity was an argument for centralisation; the others favour decentralisation.

new.s: The Gandhian Plan of 1944 is associated with:
new.x: Sriman Narayan Agarwal drew up the Gandhian Plan (1944).

new.s: For B.R. Ambedkar, the unit of the Constitution was to be the:
new.x: Ambedkar saw the village as a seat of caste domination and made the individual the unit.

new.s: Article 40, directing the State to organise village panchayats, is:
o: Part of Part IX of the Constitution
Parliament's power to modify Fundamental Rights
new.x: Article 40 is a Directive Principle in Part IV and is non-justiciable; Article 33 concerns modifying Fundamental Rights.

new.s: The 64th Amendment Bill of 1989 on panchayats failed in the:
new.x: The Bill moved by Rajiv Gandhi passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: Which Articles, giving Article 40 practical shape, came with the 73rd Amendment?
new.x: The 73rd Amendment gave Article 40 practical shape through Articles 243A, 243B and 243G.

new.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, set up after the top-down CDP, was appointed in:
new.x: The CDP (1952) ran top-down; the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in January 1957.

new.s: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, which critics say centralise local-body matters, came into force on:
new.x: The SWM Rules, 2026, under the EPA 1986, came into force on 1 April 2026; critics said on 13 May 2026 that they centralise local-body matters.

new.s: Under the principle of subsidiarity, a function moves to a higher level only when:
o: The Centre decides to withdraw it
The lowest competent level cannot perform it
Funds are not available at the district
new.x: Subsidiarity places a function at the lowest competent level; it moves up only if that level cannot do it.

new.s: Which body invoked the principle of subsidiarity for local government?
new.x: The 2nd ARC invoked subsidiarity: functions at the lowest competent level.

new.s: The term 'democratic decentralisation' was coined by the:
new.x: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) coined the term, not the Ashok Mehta Committee.

new.s: Citizens deciding matters without representatives is called:
new.x: Direct democracy means citizens decide without representatives; democratic decentralisation passes power to elected local bodies.

new.s: Sovereignty and legislative supremacy, which are not features of local self-government, belong to:
new.x: Sovereignty and legislative supremacy belong to Parliament and State legislatures, never to local bodies.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about local self-government:
1. It has a defined local area and functions.
2. It enjoys autonomy within State law.
3. It exercises judicial powers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Defined area and functions and autonomy within State law are features; judicial powers are not (Nyaya Panchayats are separate).

new.s: Who is known as the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'?
new.x: Lord Ripon, through his 1882 resolution, is the father of local self-government; Lord Mayo's 1870 resolution was about financial decentralisation.

new.s: Lord Mayo's resolution of 1870 is associated with:
o: Elected non-official majorities in local boards
new.x: Mayo's 1870 resolution gave financial decentralisation, mainly for fiscal relief; elected non-official majorities came with Ripon.

new.s: Lord Ripon's Resolution on Local Self-Government was issued on:
new.x: Ripon's resolution of 18 May 1882 treated local bodies as instruments of political and popular education.

new.s: India's municipal model, through Ripon's boards, comes from the:
new.x: India's municipal model derives from the British pattern of Ripon's boards.

new.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee held that development needed the full cooperation of the:
new.x: The Mehta Committee held local public participation indispensable for development.

new.s: The National Development Council accepted the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's report in:
new.x: The committee reported in 1957 and the NDC accepted it in January 1958.

new.s: Into how many Zilla Parishads are Andhra Pradesh's 13 Zilla Parishads being reorganised in 2026?
new.x: AP's 13 Zilla Parishads are reorganised into 28, one per district, after their terms ended on 24 September 2026.

new.s: Gram Swaraj, whose constitutional root is Article 40, is the idea of:
new.x: Gram Swaraj is Gandhi's self-reliant village republic; Article 40 is its constitutional root.

new.s: Under the revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, Centre-State funding for North-Eastern and hill States is:
new.x: RGSA funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for NE and hill States.

new.s: About what share of plan funds did Kerala's People's Plan Campaign devolve to local bodies?
new.x: About 35-40% of plan funds were devolved, not 60-70%.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about global models of local government:
1. In the British model, local councils are creatures of Parliament bound by the ultra vires rule.
2. The Scandinavian model, with strong municipalities and high local taxes, is a benchmark for fiscal decentralisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: British councils are creatures of Parliament under the ultra vires rule; Scandinavian municipalities are the fiscal-decentralisation benchmark.

new.s: The Royal Commission on Decentralisation (1907-1909) stressed which institution as the base of rural administration?
new.x: The Royal Commission on Decentralisation stressed village panchayats as the base of rural administration.

new.s: Who chaired the Royal Commission on Decentralisation after Sir Henry Primrose?
new.x: The Commission (1907-09) was chaired by Sir Henry Primrose, then C.E.H. Hobhouse.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Mayo's resolution was in 1870; Ripon's in 1882, the Royal Commission in 1907-09 and the Grow More Food campaign in 1943.

new.s: The Marthandam rural reconstruction experiment in Travancore (1921) is associated with:
new.x: Marthandam was Spencer Hatch's YMCA project; Brayne ran Gurgaon, Mayer Etawah and Dey Nilokheri.

new.s: Nilokheri, the 1948 refugee settlement experiment in East Punjab, is associated with:
new.x: Nilokheri was S.K. Dey's, not Albert Mayer's, who ran the Etawah Pilot Project.

new.s: The Firka Development Scheme (1946) in the Madras Presidency was launched by the ministry of:
new.x: The Firka Development Scheme of 1946 was launched by T. Prakasam's Madras ministry, covering Andhra areas too.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of precursor project and person is correctly matched?
new.x: Gurgaon was F.L. Brayne's; Sriniketan was Tagore's, Etawah Albert Mayer's and Sevagram Gandhi's.

new.s: The Community Development Programme began with how many pilot community projects?
new.x: The CDP began with 55 community projects as pilots.

new.s: The Community Development Programme was launched under which Five Year Plan?
new.x: The CDP was launched on 2 October 1952 within the First Five Year Plan (1951-56).

new.s: Which programme is called the 'mother of social development programmes'?
new.x: The CDP, the first major rural development programme after Independence, is called the mother of social development programmes.

new.s: The National Adult Education Programme (ages 15-35) was launched on:
new.x: NAEP began on 2 October 1978; 2 October 1952 was CDP and 2 October 1980 the nationwide IRDP.

new.s:
Arrange the following rural programmes in chronological order:
1. IRDP extended nationwide
2. National Extension Service
3. ICDS
4. National Adult Education Programme
new.x: NES (1953), ICDS (1975), NAEP (1978) and IRDP nationwide (1980).

new.s: Under the Community Development Programme, a block covered about:
new.x: The block, headed by the BDO, was the unit of planning and development of about 100 villages.

new.s: The Grow More Food campaign was started in:
new.x: The Grow More Food campaign began in 1943; its Inquiry Committee was set up in 1952.

new.s: The Grow More Food Inquiry Committee found the campaign too narrow and favoured:
new.x: Finding the campaign too narrow, the V.T. Krishnamachari committee favoured integrated village development, leading to CDP and NES.

new.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed on:
new.x: It was appointed on 16 January 1957 and reported on 24 November 1957.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee:
1. It submitted its report on 24 November 1957.
2. The National Development Council accepted it in January 1958.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the report came on 24 November 1957 and the NDC accepted it in January 1958.

new.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee reviewed which programmes?
new.x: The committee studied the CDP (1952) and NES (1953), not IRDP.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee:
1. It made the District Collector chairman of the Zila Parishad.
2. It wanted the tiers organically linked through indirect elections.
3. It recommended direct election to the Zila Parishad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Zila Parishad was indirectly elected and advisory, not directly elected.

new.s: Under the 73rd Amendment, members of the Panchayat Samiti are:
new.x: Under the 73rd Amendment Panchayat Samiti members are directly elected, unlike the Mehta model's indirect election.

new.s: In Uttar Pradesh, the Panchayat Samiti is known as the:
new.x: UP's block-level body is the Kshetra Panchayat; Gram Kachahari is Bihar's Nyaya Panchayat.

new.s: The name 'Panchayati Raj' is credited to:
new.x: The name is credited to Gandhi (Gram Swaraj); Nehru inaugurated it and Balwant Rai Mehta is its architect.

new.s: Who was Chief Minister when Andhra Pradesh adopted Panchayati Raj in 1959?
new.x: AP adopted Panchayati Raj at Shadnagar on 1 November 1959 under CM N. Sanjiva Reddy.

new.s: Which State had a four-tier Panchayati Raj pattern?
new.x: West Bengal had 4 tiers and Tamil Nadu 2; Rajasthan-AP had 3 tiers.

new.s: The phase of ascendancy of Panchayati Raj covered the years:
new.x: Ascendancy was 1959-1964; decline was 1969-1983.

new.s: The phase of decline of Panchayati Raj is dated to:
new.x: The decline phase ran 1969-1983, before revival after the Ashok Mehta Committee.

new.s: The K. Santhanam Committee of 1963 dealt with:
new.x: Santhanam dealt with PR Finances (1963) and PR Elections (1965); Nyaya Panchayats was G.R. Rajagopalan.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of committee and subject is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: G. Ramachandran (1969) dealt with Training Centres; Nyaya Panchayats was G.R. Rajagopalan (1962).

new.s: Bihar's Nyaya Panchayat is called the:
new.x: Bihar's judicial panchayat is the Gram Kachahari.

new.s: Which committee wanted Nyaya Panchayats kept separate from development panchayats and presided over by a qualified judge?
new.x: Ashok Mehta wanted separate Nyaya Panchayats under a qualified judge; Singhvi wanted them for clusters of villages.

new.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee submitted its report in:
new.x: Appointed in December 1977, it reported in August 1978 with 132 recommendations.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ashok Mehta Committee:
1. It was appointed in December 1977.
2. It made 132 recommendations.
3. It was appointed by the Rajiv Gandhi government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; it was appointed by the Janata government of Morarji Desai.

new.s: The Mandal Panchayat proposed by the Ashok Mehta Committee was to cover a population of:
new.x: The Mandal Panchayat was a group of villages with 15,000-20,000 people.

new.s: Which State, under its Panchayat Act of 1973, held panchayat polls in June 1978 on Ashok Mehta lines?
new.x: West Bengal (Panchayat Act 1973; polls June 1978), Karnataka and AP adopted the Committee's ideas.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct in comparing the Balwant Rai Mehta and Ashok Mehta Committees?
o: Balwant Rai Mehta – block as the unit
Ashok Mehta – district as the unit
Balwant Rai Mehta recommended constitutional status
new.x: Balwant Rai Mehta did not propose constitutional status; Ashok Mehta recommended it.

new.s: The report of the G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985) was titled:
o: Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation Programmes
Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development
Study of Community Projects and National Extension Service
new.x: That was the G.V.K. Rao report; 'Revitalisation of PRIs' was L.M. Singhvi's.

new.s: The G.V.K. Rao Committee of 1985 was set up by the:
new.x: G.V.K. Rao was a Planning Commission committee; Gadgil was the Congress Party's and Thungon a Parliament sub-committee.

new.s: The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) was appointed by the government of:
new.x: The Singhvi Committee was appointed by the Rajiv Gandhi government in 1986.

new.s: The L.M. Singhvi Committee described the Gram Sabha as the:
new.x: Singhvi called the Gram Sabha the embodiment of direct democracy; 'grass without roots' was G.V.K. Rao's phrase.

new.s: The P.K. Thungon Committee's list of Panchayati Raj subjects later became the:
new.x: Thungon's list of PR subjects led to the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects).

new.s: Unlike the G.V.K. Rao Committee, the L.M. Singhvi Committee focused on which key unit?
o: Gram Sabha and viable gram panchayats
new.x: G.V.K. Rao centred on the district and Zila Parishad; Singhvi on the Gram Sabha and viable gram panchayats.

new.s: The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) dealt with:
new.x: Dinesh Goswami (1990) was on electoral reforms, not a Panchayati Raj committee.

new.s: Which of these Panchayati Raj committees was the latest?
new.x: Dantwala (1978), Hanumantha Rao (1984), G.V.K. Rao (1985), Gadgil (1988).

new.s: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Bill of 1989 dealt with:
new.x: The 65th Bill was the Nagarpalika Bill for municipalities; the 64th dealt with panchayats.

new.s: What was the fate of the 65th Amendment (Nagarpalika) Bill in 1989?
o: Lapsed on dissolution of the Lok Sabha
Referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
new.x: Like the 64th Bill, the 65th Bill was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in 1989.

new.s: The panchayat bill of 1990 was moved by the National Front government of:
new.x: The National Front government of V.P. Singh moved the 1990 bill.

new.s: The National Front government's panchayat bill of 1990:
o: Was defeated for lack of special majority
Was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
Lapsed when the Lok Sabha was dissolved
new.x: The 1990 bill lapsed on dissolution of the Lok Sabha; the Narasimha Rao bills went to a JPC and passed in December 1992.

new.s: The modified panchayat bills introduced by the Narasimha Rao government in September 1991 were scrutinised by a:
new.x: The September 1991 bills went to a Joint Parliamentary Committee and were passed in December 1992.

new.s: Parliament passed the Narasimha Rao government's panchayat bills in:
new.x: They were passed in December 1992; the 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993.

new.s: The 64th Amendment Bill drew on the recommendations of which committees?
o: Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta and Dantwala
Hanumantha Rao, Dantwala and G.V.K. Rao
new.x: The 64th Bill (July 1989) was based on the Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil committees.

new.s: Under Article 243D(3), the seats reserved for women in Panchayats are at least:
new.x: Article 243D(3) reserves at least one-third of seats for women.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a provision of the 73rd Amendment?
o: 243B(2) – middle tier may be skipped below 20 lakh population
new.x: Regular remuneration to members is not a provision; 243K, 243J and 243B(2) are.

new.s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule?
new.x: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment, lists 29 subjects.

new.s: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on:
new.x: National Panchayati Raj Day is 24 April, the day the 73rd Amendment came into force in 1993.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959 began which structure?
new.x: The 1959 Act began the three-tier structure in AP on 1 November 1959.

new.s: Which Andhra Pradesh law consolidated the village-panchayat law?
o: AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959
new.x: The AP Gram Panchayats Act, 1964 consolidated village-panchayat law.

new.s: The national rural development institute NIRDPR is located in:
new.x: NIRDPR is in Hyderabad.
